newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Akzo sets 10 pct ROI target for fibres.
newsitem.headline: Akzo sets 10 pct ROI target for fibres.

text.p: Chemical group Akzo Nobel NV said on Thursday it planned further restructuring at its troubled fibres unit aimed at generating a return on investment of 10 percent within two to three years.

"We must at least make good our financing costs...ultimately we have to generate a return on invested capital of 10 percent and we are still very far from that," finance director Jean den Hoed told a results news conference.
Den Hoed said that although second-quarter results at fibres had risen five million guilders to 20 million, the division was still plagued by global industry overcapacity.
"Despite all the measures taken in the past, operating income still totals only a scant two percent of sales...not even sufficient to compensate for the financing charges," he said.
"We must at least cover the financial costs, and really we should generate a 10 percent return on invested capital," Den Hoed added.
He said Akzo would have to implement further internal cost-cutting but that he could not yet detail the restructuring measures to be taken.
However, job losses could not be ruled out, he said.
